styles.label: History
styles.blurb: The Acropolis, the Ancient Agora and the Acropolis Museum.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Tavernas, souvlaki and long dinners in Plaka and Koukaki.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: Tram to the coast for a swim and a seaside lunch.

stays.why: Old-town lanes right under the Acropolis; walk to the Ancient Agora and most central sights.
Central and well connected: metro to the airport and Piraeus, walk to the National Garden and Plaka.
Flea market, street food and the metro hub; lively at night and close to the Ancient Agora.
Quiet residential streets near the Acropolis Museum with good local tavernas; often better value.

food: Try souvlaki and gyros from a grill house: cheap, fast and everywhere. Expect about €3–5 for a wrap.
Order meze to share: tzatziki, fava, grilled octopus and small fried fish. Two or three plates per person is plenty.
Eat dinner late like locals, roughly 21:00–23:00. Many tavernas are quiet before 20:00.
Look for a taverna with a handwritten menu and local diners rather than a photo menu on the street.
In summer, eat lunch by the sea on the coast and keep the centre for dinner. Book popular places ahead on weekends.
more_time: Take a day trip to Cape Sounion for the Temple of Poseidon and a sunset over the sea. Check bus times on the day.
Ferries from Piraeus reach the islands; a day trip to Aegina is the easiest. Book ahead in summer.
Add a half-day at the National Archaeological Museum, then wander the Exarchia streets nearby.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Acropolis, the museum and the old town at an easy pace. Add a night for a coast or island day.

month_notes: January: cold and damp, highs near 12°C. Pack a warm layer and expect some rain days.
February: still cool, around 14°C by day. Quiet sights and low prices.
March: mild at 16°C with about 7 rain days. Good for walking the ruins without heat.
April: pleasant at 20°C. One of the best months for sightseeing.
May: warm at 25°C and mostly dry. Great for both the centre and the coast.
June: hot at 30°C. Start sightseeing early and rest in the afternoon shade.
July: very hot, highs near 33°C. Go out early and late; the Acropolis is exposed.
August: as hot as July and busy. Book ahead and carry water.
September: warm at 29°C and drier. A strong month for beaches and ruins.
October: comfortable at 23°C. Good light and fewer crowds.
November: cooler at 19°C with more rain days. Bring a rain jacket.
December: cool at 14°C and wetter. Festive centre, short daylight.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean climate: hot, dry summers and mild, wetter winters. Spring and autumn are the sweet spots.

items.title: Best time: April to June and September to October
items.text: Days around 20–29°C with little rain. Ideal for ruins, walking and the coast.

items.title: Summer is very hot (July–August)
items.text: Highs near 33°C and few rain days. Sightseeing is hard at midday; go early or late.

items.title: Wettest in winter
items.text: December to February have about 7–8 rain days a month. Showers are usually short.

items.title: Cool winters
items.text: January highs near 12°C and lows around 5°C. Bring a warm coat for evenings.

items.title: Sea season
items.text: Beach weather runs roughly June to September, warmest in July and August.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Sun hat and sunscreen for summer; a light rain jacket and warm layer for winter; comfortable shoes for marble and stone paths.

transit.best: Metro for the centre and airport; walk in Plaka and Monastiraki.

modes.text: 3 lines, running about 05:30–00:30, later on Friday and Saturday nights. One OASA ticket costs €1.20 and covers metro, tram and bus with transfers for 90 minutes.
Buses and the tram use the same €1.20 OASA ticket. The airport express bus X93/X95 costs €5.50.
Taxis are yellow; insist on the meter and expect shared rides at busy times. Uber and Bolt work in Athens and help avoid fare haggling.
Driving in the centre is hard: narrow streets, little parking and heavy traffic. Skip it for city days.
Best way around Plaka, Monastiraki and Syntagma. Wear shoes with grip for marble and stone paths.
Piraeus port is about 10 km from the centre, with ferries to the islands. Reach it by metro.
